extracted.intended_audience: government policymakers, central government regulatory oversight bodies, regulatory agencies, and officials responsible for regulatory policy and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: A formal OECD Recommendation setting out principles and detailed guidance for designing, assessing and governing regulation across whole-of-government systems, including impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, oversight, review and international cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit at the highest political level to an explicit whole-of-government policy for regulatory quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy should have clear objectives and frameworks for implementation to ensure that, if regulation is used, the economic, social and environmental benefits justify the costs, distributional effects are considered and the net benefits are maximised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a continuous policy cycle for regulatory decision-making (identify objectives → design → evaluation); use regulation only when appropriate; maintain a regulatory management system including ex ante impact assessment and ex post evaluation; articulate regulatory policy goals, strategies and benefits clearly; systematically review the stock of regulations periodically; develop, implement and evaluate communications strategy. Adopt an integrated approach across levels and sectors; consider impacts on competitiveness and growth; commit to apply regulatory policy when preparing sectoral regulations; monitor impacts and develop programmes to reduce administrative and compliance costs. Governments should develop strategic capacity, issue a formal binding policy statement with guidelines for tools/procedures, assess institutional frameworks and resources, prefer performance-based regulation, clearly identify ministers' responsibilities and consider assigning a specific Minister for oversight (monitoring coordination, reporting performance, identifying system-wide improvements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to open government principles: transparency and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to principles of open government, including transparency and participation in the regulatory process to ensure that regulation serves the public interest and is informed by the legitimate needs of those interested in and affected by regulation. Provide meaningful opportunities (including online) for the public to contribute to draft proposals and supporting analysis; ensure regulations are comprehensible and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a clear policy identifying how open and balanced public consultation will take place. Actively engage all relevant stakeholders; design consultation to maximise information quality and effectiveness; consult on all aspects of impact assessment and use RIA as part of consultation; make available to the public, as far as possible, all relevant material from regulatory dossiers including supporting analyses and reasons for decisions; structure reviews around needs of affected parties and cooperate with them on prioritisation and simplification proposals; evaluate competitive effects of regulation. Introduce regular performance assessments of regulations and regulatory systems and communicate results. Ensure inspection/enforcement policies respect legitimate rights, maximise net public benefits and avoid unnecessary burdens. Maintain a complete, up-to-date, freely accessible searchable legislative/regulatory database. Require drafting in plain language and provide clear compliance guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish oversight mechanisms and institutions for regulatory policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish mechanisms and institutions to actively provide oversight of regulatory policy procedures and goals, support and implement regulatory policy, and thereby foster regulatory quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a standing regulatory oversight body close to the centre of government (adapted to governance system); set its authority in mandate/statute/executive order; ensure independence from political influence in technical functions. Tasks should include quality control of impact assessments (return inadequate ones), examine potential for more effective regulation, contribute to systematic improvement of regulatory policy application, coordinate ex post evaluation, provide training and guidance on impact assessment and improvement strategies. The oversight body's performance, including review of impact assessments, should be periodically assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) early in policy development
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate Regulatory Impact Assessment (RIA) into the early stages of the policy process for formulation of new regulatory proposals; clearly identify policy goals and evaluate if regulation is necessary and how it can be most effective and efficient in achieving those goals; consider non-regulatory means and tradeoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt ex ante impact assessment proportional to regulation significance and include benefit–cost analyses considering economic, social and environmental impacts and distributional effects. Require identification of a specific policy need and objective (market failure, protection of rights). Consider alternatives (regulatory, non-regulatory), including baseline/no-action. For significant impacts, make assessments quantitative where possible and include qualitative descriptions where quantification is difficult (equity, distributional effects). Make RIA publicly available in suitable form and in time for stakeholder input; use RIA in consultation. Ensure regulation seeks to enhance competition and consumer welfare; evaluate and limit adverse effects on competition. When assessing, evaluate long-term/spatial impacts, international instrument adoption, and impacts on SMEs (minimise administrative/compliance costs). Support RIA with policies, training, guidance and quality control for data collection/use and integrate it early in policy development across agencies and centre of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct systematic programme reviews of the stock of significant regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct systematic programme reviews of the stock of significant regulation against clearly defined policy goals, including consideration of costs and benefits, to ensure regulations remain up to date, cost-justified, cost-effective and consistent and deliver intended objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate RIA methods into review/revision programmes with explicit objectives to improve efficiency/effectiveness and reduce regulatory costs. Schedule reviews to assess all significant regulation systematically over time, prioritise identifying ineffective regulation and those with significant economic impacts, consider permanent review mechanisms (review clauses, sunsetting). Assess coherence with economic, social and environmental policies. Include administrative simplification programmes with measurements of aggregate burdens and consider explicit targets. Complement quantitative methods with qualitative ones. Employ IT and one-stop shops for licences/permits to reduce transaction costs and streamline interactions between citizens/businesses and government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly publish reports on regulatory policy and reform performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly publish reports on the performance of regulatory policy and reform programmes and the public authorities applying the regulations; include information on how tools such as RIA, public consultation and reviews are functioning in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review effectiveness of programmes to improve regulatory delivery inside government against clearly identified public service delivery objectives. Design and assess data collection and information management to ensure high-quality information for reports while avoiding unnecessary administrative burdens. Promote external review functions including stakeholder and civil society input; have RIA assessments periodically evaluated by an independent third party. Evaluate simplification/reform programmes for public value delivered (focus on outcomes/effects for society ahead of quantifying administrative burdens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop consistent policy on regulatory agencies' roles and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a consistent policy covering the role and functions of regulatory agencies to provide confidence that decisions are objective, impartial and consistent, without conflict of interest, bias or improper influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation granting regulatory authority should clearly state objectives and powers. Compile and maintain a public register of all government entities exercising regulatory functions, including statutory objectives and instruments administered. Consider independent regulatory agencies where needed to maintain public confidence, ensure competitive neutrality, or where decisions have significant economic impacts. Require public accountability mechanisms defining how agencies discharge responsibilities with expertise, integrity and objectivity. Require agencies to follow regulatory policy including stakeholder engagement and undertaking RIA when developing draft laws, guidelines and soft law. Subject agency performance to regular external evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure effective systems for review of legality and procedural fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the effectiveness of systems for the review of the legality and procedural fairness of regulations and of decisions made by bodies empowered to issue regulatory sanctions; ensure citizens and businesses have access to review at reasonable cost and receive decisions in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready access for citizens and businesses to challenge exercise of public authority, especially regulatory sanctions. Include the right to appeal regulators' decisions on legal grounds including procedural fairness and due process; allow challenge in court of statutory provisions against higher legal norms (including constitutional). Appeals should, in principle, be heard by a separate authority than the one making the original decision. Establish standard time periods for administrative decisions where appropriate so applicants can expect timely decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply risk assessment, management and communication strategies as appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: As appropriate apply risk assessment, risk management, and risk communication strategies to the design and implementation of regulations to ensure that regulation is targeted and effective; regulators should assess how regulations will be given effect and design responsive implementation and enforcement strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include risk strategy in public statement underpinning regulatory reform; develop and regularly update guidance on methodologies for risk assessment, management and communication. Build accountable review systems for risk assessments on major proposals (e.g., expert peer review). Evaluate risk strategies for effectiveness in identifying/informing actions to avoid or mitigate catastrophic/systemic risks and minimise unintended consequences and 'risk–risk' tradeoffs; incorporate lessons from past events. Consider risk-based approaches in design and enforcement to increase likelihood of compliance and minimise costs. Require regulators to develop, implement and review compliance strategies against risk-based criteria. Where the precautionary principle is applied, build an accountable system for review as scientific information becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote regulatory coherence across supranational, national and sub-national levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate promote regulatory coherence through coordination mechanisms between supranational, national and sub‑national levels of government; identify cross‑cutting regulatory issues to promote coherence and avoid duplication or conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design coordination mechanisms for all levels, including harmonisation measures or mutual recognition agreements; develop tools to diagnose cross-cutting issues and identify/reform overlapping regulations (including with supranational organisations). Capitalise on proximity of sub-national governments to firms/citizens to develop effective consultation procedures and reflect local needs. Promote information sharing and transparency between levels and effective use of benchmarks. Disseminate innovative local regulatory practices. Facilitate local variations and experimentation when nationally beneficial. Encourage supranational bodies with rule-making powers to consider and apply relevant aspects of this Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster regulatory management capacity and performance at sub-national levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster the development of regulatory management capacity and performance at sub‑national levels of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support implementation of regulatory policy/programmes at sub‑national level to reduce regulatory costs/barriers that limit competition and investment. Promote programmes to assess and reduce compliance costs where simplification is urgent to avoid legal vacuum, inconsistencies, duplication and overlap. Promote procedures at sub‑national level to assess where reform/simplification is most urgent. Ensure regulatory charges are set for cost recovery, not to yield revenue. Support capacity-building through e‑government and administrative simplification and relevant HR policies. Use incentives to foster RIA use by sub‑national governments to consider impacts of new/amending regulations and avoid barriers to internal markets. Develop incentives for horizontal coordination across jurisdictions and mechanisms for resolving disputes; prevent conflicts of interest by separating sub‑national governments' roles as regulators and service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider international standards and cooperation when developing regulatory measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing regulatory measures, give consideration to all relevant international standards and frameworks for cooperation in the same field and, where appropriate, their likely effects on parties outside the jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise international regulatory cooperation as integral to systemic risk management and long‑term planning. Evaluate whether adoption of common international instruments will efficiently address policy issues and foster global coherence with minimal disruption. Act in accordance with international treaty obligations (e.g., ILO, UN, WTO/GATT) which may require nondiscriminatory treatment. Cooperate with other countries to promote development and support of International Regulatory Co‑operation; contribute to international fora (including private/semi-private) to foster diffusion of good practices. Avoid duplication where recognition of existing regulations/standards would achieve objectives at lower cost. Ensure consultation processes are open to submissions from foreign and domestic interests and consider international contexts when formulating proposals.
